## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design an isolated TLS rotation workflow that leverages cert-manager, RBAC, and policy enforcement while producing auditable logs.

## Key Concepts
- Deployments, InitContainers, and probes for reliable pod lifecycle management
- Secrets and Bearer token authentication for secure credential handling
- cert-manager integration for automated certificate rotation testing
- PVC-based logging for persistent audit trails
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control and network segmentation

## Trade-offs
- **Simplicity vs. Security**: Using a single ServiceAccount with broad permissions simplifies implementation but increases blast radius if compromised
- **PVC vs. Sidecar**: A sidecar container offers simpler log shipping but adds resource overhead; a PVC requires external log rotation
- **Polling vs. Watching**: Polling with a cron-style schedule is less efficient than watching but avoids the complexity of setting up a custom controller with informers
- **Egress Control**: NetworkPolicy adds security but increases operational complexity and requires CNI support

kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["secrets"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
  - apiGroups: ["cert-manager.io"]
    resources: ["certificates"]
    verbs: ["get", "create", "delete"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: cert-verifier
    namespace: cert-verifier
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: cert-verifier
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-credentials
  namespace: cert-verifier
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: "<bearer-token>"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier-logs
  namespace: cert-verifier
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cert-verifier
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cert-verifier
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: cert-verifier
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: alpine:latest
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - apk add --no-cache curl jq
          volumeMounts:
            - name: workdir
              mountPath: /work
      containers:
        - name: verifier
          image: alpine:latest
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              apk add --no-cache curl jq
              while true; do
                # Watch secrets, check expiry, rotate, post digest
                sleep 3600
              done
          volumeMounts:
            - name: workdir
              mountPath: /work
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /var/log
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthy
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
        - name: workdir
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: cert-verifier-logs
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier-egress
  namespace: cert-verifier
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cert-verifier
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              name: audit-system
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: audit-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443
```

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped RBAC for fine-grained access control

data:

apiVersion: v1

kind: PersistentVolumeClaim

  namespace: example
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: audit-agent
  namespace: example
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: audit-agent
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl jq && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
      containers:
      - name: auditor
        image: your-audit-image:latest
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; do audit.sh; sleep 60; done"]
        env:

        - name: AUTH_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: audit-auth
              key: token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
        - name: baseline
          mountPath: /baseline
          readOnly: true
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: audit-logs
      - name: tools
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: baseline
        configMap:
          name: audit-baseline
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: example
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: audit-system
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: collector
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **Pros**: Namespace isolation ensures audit agents don't interfere; NetworkPolicy provides security; PVC enables log persistence for compliance
- **Cons**: Each namespace requires separate Deployment (use Operator/Controller to automate); InitContainer adds startup latency; per-namespace RBAC management overhead increases with cluster size

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests knowledge of namespace-scoped governance primitives (LimitRange, ResourceQuota) and how defaults affect scheduling, QoS, and multi-tenant fairness in CKAD.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace scoping
- LimitRange defaultRequests/defaultLimits
- ResourceQuota hard limits
- Pod scheduling under quotas
- Impact on autoscaling and experimentation

## Code Example
```yaml
# Namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: test-ns
---
# LimitRange
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: default-limits
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    type: Container
---
# ResourceQuota
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: resource-quota
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  hard:
    pods: "10"
    requests.cpu: "1"
    requests.memory: 1Gi
    limits.cpu: "2"
    limits.memory: 2Gi
---
# Deployment (inherits defaults)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample-app
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: sample-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: sample-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

## Trade-offs
**Advantages:**
- Prevents resource starvation across namespaces
- Enforces fair resource distribution
- Automatic defaults reduce configuration errors
- Provides cost control boundaries

**Considerations:**
- Too restrictive limits can hinder scaling
- Default limits may be overprovisioned for small workloads
- ResourceQuota refusals require manual quota increases
- May impact autoscaling behavior if quotas are too tight

**Best Practices:**
- Set conservative defaults but allow overrides
- Monitor quota utilization regularly
- Use separate quotas for production vs development
- Consider pod priority classes for critical workloads

## Why This Matters
This question tests critical CKAD competencies: initializing pods with InitContainers, configuring volume mounts for data sharing, implementing zero-downtime deployments, and ensuring availability during disruptions with PodDisruptionBudgets.

## Key Concepts

- **InitContainer**: Runs to completion before main containers start. Uses the same volume mounts to share data with the main container. Multiple init containers run sequentially.

- **Volume Mounts**: The ConfigMap is mounted at `/config` for the init container to access `cache-base`. An `emptyDir` volume shares `/var/cache` between init and main containers.

- **RollingUpdate maxUnavailable: 0**: Critical for zero-downtime updates. Ensures all 3 pods update one at a time, with a new pod fully ready before the old one terminates.

- **PodDisruptionBudget minAvailable: 2**: With 3 replicas, guarantees at least 2 pods remain healthy during voluntary disruptions (node drains, API server issues). This prevents service degradation.

## Common Pitfalls

1. **Missing volumeMounts in init container** - InitContainer cannot access volumes without explicit mountPath
2. **maxUnavailable set to 1** - Can cause brief unavailability during rolling updates
3. **PDB selector mismatch** - Must match the Deployment's pod selector exactly
4. **Forgetting emptyDir for /var/cache** - Without a volume, /var/cache would be lost on container restart

          volumeMounts:

            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "500m"
              memory: "256Mi"
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
          livenessProbe:

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical CKAD skills: dynamic configuration via ConfigMaps, per-namespace isolation, InitContainers, health checks, logging, and network policy considerations.

## Key Concepts

- **Namespace-scoped ConfigMaps**: Enable dynamic feature flags without pod restarts
- **InitContainers**: Provide bootstrap tooling (curl) before the main container starts
- **Conditional sidecars**: Driven by ConfigMap values to enable canary deployments
- **Readiness and liveness probes**: Ensure controller and application health
- **PVC-backed logs**: Provide persistent storage for debugging and audit trails
- **NetworkPolicies**: Enforce zero-trust networking by restricting egress to known endpoints

## Trade-offs

| Aspect | Consideration |
|--------|----------------|
| **Polling Interval** | Frequent polls increase API load; infrequent polls delay flag propagation |
| **ConfigMap Updates** | Applications must watch or periodically read the ConfigMap to detect changes |
| **Sidecar Overhead** | Running a sidecar even when disabled consumes resources; consider whether the main container can react to flag changes directly |
| **Egress Restriction** | Locking down NetworkPolicy requires knowing all upstream dependencies upfront |
| **Log Persistence** | PVCs add operational complexity and cost; consider external logging solutions for production |

## Minimal YAML Skeleton

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: feature-flags
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-flags
  namespace: feature-flags
data:
  flags.json: '{}'
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: logs-pvc
  namespace: feature-flags
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: flag-poller
  namespace: feature-flags
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: flag-poller
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: flag-poller
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-curl
          image: curlimages/curl:latest
          command: ['sh', '-c', 'cp /usr/bin/curl /tools/curl']
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
      containers:
        - name: poller
          image: your-poller-image:latest
          command: ['/bin/sh', '-c', 'while true; do curl -s $FLAGS_API > /config/flags.json; sleep 60; done']
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /config
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
        - name: sidecar
          image: your-sidecar-image:latest
          env:
            - name: FEATURE_ENABLED
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: feature-flags
                  key: enabled
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: feature-flags
        - name: tools
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: logs-pvc
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: flags-egress-policy
  namespace: feature-flags
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: flag-poller
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: flags-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
```

This design balances flexibility with operational simplicity, making it well-suited for Kubernetes feature management in multi-tenant environments.
